thesis.counterparty: Over-leveraged traders (documented up to 100-125x on major venues in 2025 cascades) on the losing side of the initiating move, whose positions are force-closed by the exchange's liquidation/ADL engine at the prevailing market price regardless of their own view — they are structurally forced to keep selling (or buying, if short) into the move, which is the flow a same-direction entrant captures.
thesis.evidence: arxiv.org/html/2608.03616 ('Measuring the engine of a liquidation cascade: subcritical branching inside a first-order transition'): reports that 87.8% of all post-onset forced selling in the studied BTC cascade occurred in the first 30 minutes (96.5% within an hour) -- i.e. liquidation-driven forced flow is real, mechanically distinct from discretionary flow, and heavily front-loaded (this is the caveat built into the prediction above). coinchange.io Nov-2025 cascade writeup: reports 'nearly $2 billion in leveraged liquidations' over 24h, '396,000 traders were liquidated, the highest single-day count of 2025', and '85% being long liquidations' during the Nov 2025 BTC drawdown from $126,080 to $81,600 (35%) -- documents that liquidation-driven, heavily one-sided forced flow at scale is a recurring, current (2025) phenomenon on crypto perpetuals, not a 2022-only artifact. research/swarm/kb/owner_trades/api_closed_pnl.json (local, descriptive only, not statistical evidence per the probe): the owner's single largest realized-PnL trade in the 819-row 2022-2023 record (+$1,089.62, u100TRYBUSD, opened 2022-11-10T07:53:39 UTC per research/swarm/runs/2026-09-20-0300/theses/owner_record_probe.json 'concentration' block) falls inside the Nov 8-11 2022 FTX-contagion deleveraging window that also drove ~$7,373 of the account's ~$4,857 final cumulative realized PnL from just the 99 trades opened in November 2022 (same probe file, 'nov_2022_window_note') -- consistent with, but not proof of, a forced-deleveraging-driven directional-flow mechanism motivating this thesis; the probe explicitly says this window match is descriptive, not a statistical claim.
thesis.mechanism: A 1h bar with an abnormally large return (|z|>2.5 vs its own 20-bar rolling volatility) plus an abnormal volume spike (z>2.0 vs its own 20-bar rolling volume) is a proxy for a forced-deleveraging / liquidation-cascade event: an exchange's liquidation engine (and auto-deleveraging queue) closes over-leveraged positions on the losing side of the move at market price, irrespective of whether that price is fair-value-justified. That forced flow is price-insensitive and one-directional by construction, so it mechanically extends the move beyond what discretionary/fundamental order flow alone would produce, for a short window after the flagged bar, before the forced-selling/buying pool exhausts.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 6 (liquidation-cascade reversion) died because the operator faded high-vol bars expecting mean reversion and found 'high-vol bars CONTINUE, don't revert.' This thesis takes the opposite, continuation-direction bet that row 6's own finding implies, rather than repeating the reversion bet with different parameters.

Row 80 (tape_snapback) was refuted for the same economic bet as row 6 (continuation, not reversion) but its kill reason was a fee-math defect: it misapplied the maker-blend rate to a taker entry, understating real round-trip cost by roughly half. This spec uses fee_math.C_BPS (11.5bps, includes the measured 4.5bps adverse-selection term) unmodified for the cost gate rather than re-deriving a cheaper rate by hand.

Row 5 (market-neutral cross-sectional momentum) is a continuous, always-in-market basket strategy needing ~100-470 names and dies from short-leg survivorship. This thesis is event-triggered (fires only on a flagged abnormal bar), single-symbol at a time, no cross-sectional basket, and no short-leg symmetry requirement.

Row 13 (BTC-TSM 28,5) is unconditional trend-following on a fixed 28-day lookback that doesn't beat buy-and-hold. This thesis is conditioned on a specific forced-liquidation proxy event, holds hours not weeks, and its counterparty is a mechanical liquidation-engine flow, not a generic trend/carry premium.

Row 33 (BTC/ETH Donchian-ensemble trend, paper) was a continuous channel-breakout trend system the owner declined to take live. This is a single discrete-event trigger (cascade bar) with a short fixed max-hold, not a continuously-in-market trend ensemble.

thesis.prediction: On 1h closed bars for BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE (mr_edge dataset, train era), entering in the direction of a cascade-flagged bar (return z < -2.5 and volume z > 2.0 -> short; return z > 2.5 and volume z > 2.0 -> long) and holding up to 6 bars (6h) nets positive expectancy after the 11.5bps round-trip cost (fee_math.C_BPS) at n>=30, with bootstrap CI95 of net bps (bootstrap_ci.mean_ci) excluding zero, and observed win rate >= p*(200)=52.875% (fee_math.p_star). Falsified if net bps CI includes/is below zero or observed WR < 52.875% for the 200bps TP leg. Caveat carried honestly into the spec: an arxiv analysis of a 2025 BTC cascade found 87.8% of post-onset forced selling completes within the first 30 minutes of cascade onset (96.5% within an hour) — by the time a signal fires on a closed 1h bar most of the forced flow for that specific bar is already done, so this thesis is betting on either (a) the tail of that flow plus discretionary momentum-chasers, or (b) a second wave in a correlated symbol lagging the leader; the screen's CI is the actual adjudicator of whether either effect survives, not this prose.
thesis.signal_py:
"""
owner_record_liq_cascade_continuation signal.
Signals(df) -> pd.Series in {-1,0,1}, computed on CLOSED bars only.
Fires -1 (short) on a bar whose return is an abnormal negative outlier vs its own trailing
volatility AND whose volume is an abnormal positive outlier vs its own trailing volume
(liquidation-cascade-down proxy); fires +1 (long) on the mirrored abnormal-up case.
All rolling stats use only data up to and including the current closed bar (rolling(),
no shift(-k), no future index access) -> passes the whole-prefix causality check.
"""
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

ROLL = 20
RET_Z_THRESH = 2.5
VOL_Z_THRESH = 2.0


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    ret = df["close"].pct_change()
    roll_std = ret.rolling(ROLL, min_periods=ROLL).std()
    vol_mean = df["volume"].rolling(ROLL, min_periods=ROLL).mean()
    vol_std = df["volume"].rolling(ROLL, min_periods=ROLL).std()

    ret_z = ret / roll_std.replace(0, np.nan)
    vol_z = (df["volume"] - vol_mean) / vol_std.replace(0, np.nan)

    cascade_down = (ret_z < -RET_Z_THRESH) & (vol_z > VOL_Z_THRESH)
    cascade_up = (ret_z > RET_Z_THRESH) & (vol_z > VOL_Z_THRESH)

    sig = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
    sig[cascade_down.fillna(False)] = -1
    sig[cascade_up.fillna(False)] = 1
    return sig

spec.doa_line: Kill if, after n>=30 train-era signals across the 5-symbol universe, bootstrap_ci.mean_ci on net bps (after fee_math.C_BPS=11.5bps) includes zero, OR observed win rate < fee_math.p_star(200)=52.875%, OR the +-20% tp_bps robustness read (STANDARDS #9) flips net_bps_mean sign between the +20% and -20% variants.
